sections.title: Signing up for a weekend cooking session

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: The kitchen is running a short class on making packed lunches. I can put you on the list and let you know what is supplied.

script.speaker: Participant
script.text: All right. Let’s go through the details.

script.text: What have you put down for the booking surname?

script.speaker: Tutor

script.speaker: Participant
script.text: What should I write for the class day?

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Your class is on Sunday. Saturday’s session is for a separate group.

script.speaker: Participant
script.text: And what is the start time?

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: We start at 11:20. The earlier group will be clearing the benches just before that.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: The first demonstration is fifteen minutes. After that the group works in pairs.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Use the green bucket for food waste. The grey one is for packaging.

script.speaker: Tutor

sections.title: The layout of a glass exhibition

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The exhibition has four rooms around the central junction. North is at the top of your plan. I will describe where to begin and what can be touched.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The colour room is east of the junction. Follow the path on the right to a wide doorway.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The tool gallery is south of the junction, near the bottom of the plan. Its entrance is next to the long bench.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The window display is west of the junction. The left-hand room has the tallest opening.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The workshop screen is north of the junction, towards the top. It separates the viewing area from the working room.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Touch only the objects on the sample table. The old pieces in cases are not part of the handling activity.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Look at the frame holding two coloured sheets. The light behind it makes the overlap easier to see.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The first film lasts nine minutes. You can join the group again at the junction afterwards.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: There is a card beside the door that explains the symbols on the displays. You may borrow one.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: A member of staff will demonstrate the lamp. Wait for them rather than trying to move it yourself.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Put borrowed cards in the basket on the way out. This makes them available for the next visitors.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: You can stay after the guided visit. Please keep drinks outside the rooms and return borrowed materials to the entrance.

sections.title: Comparing two displays of water use

script.speaker: Fiona
script.text: Our visual design exercise asks how easily visitors can compare water use from a graph. We need two designs that show the same figures.

script.speaker: Marc
script.text: All right. Let’s go through the details.

script.speaker: Fiona
script.text: Ask for the month with the highest use. We are not asking which design they prefer or which number they remember later.

script.speaker: Marc
script.text: Keep the figures shown the same. The position of the labels can change, and the title can be moved to make room.

script.speaker: Fiona
script.text: Write down the first answer before discussing it. If you ask for a reason first, the person may change the answer while speaking.

script.speaker: Marc
script.text: Fiona will draw the graphs. Marc will check the source numbers and Ada will arrange a room.

script.speaker: Fiona
script.text: Marc will check the source numbers. We want to be sure the two printed designs show the same values.

script.speaker: Marc
script.text: Ada will reserve the room. She is choosing a space where a visitor can look at one graph at a time.

script.speaker: Fiona
script.text: Use the same board for both graphs. A change in height would affect what people can see comfortably.

script.speaker: Marc
script.text: Keep the unused graph in a folder. People should see one design before being shown the other.

script.speaker: Fiona
script.text: Record whether the answer was given without a prompt. We can separate those answers from cases where help was needed.

script.speaker: Marc
script.text: Put the reason in a short note next to the answer. Do not try to rewrite it as a rating.

script.speaker: Fiona
script.text: If people interpret a label differently from what we expected, keep that response. It may tell us what needs to be changed.

sections.title: Comparing the rate at which containers leak

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: A leak can appear to be the same size in two containers while the amount of liquid lost differs. We will compare the loss under conditions that can be reproduced.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Fill each container to the same marked level. The starting height of the water can affect the way it leaves.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Put a jug below the container to collect the escaping water. Check that it is stable before the trial starts.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Start the timer as soon as the outlet is opened. Do not include the time spent setting up.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Measure the amount after the same interval. A longer collection period would change the result.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Check the diameter of each opening. If the openings differ, you cannot attribute the change only to container shape.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Place a piece of tape at the final water level. It is useful to have a visible record after pouring out the rest.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Place the container on a level surface. Otherwise the water height at the outlet may differ from the marked height.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Dry the outside before checking the mass. Water left on the surface could affect the reading.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Do a comparison with the outlet closed. It helps show whether there was another source of water loss.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Put the starting and finishing values in the same table. The difference is easier to verify when both are available.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: The result describes a particular container and starting level. State those conditions before extending the conclusion to another situation.
